project.name: BD Home Hunt
project.description: Realtime collaborative house-hunting dashboard for Bronwynne & Dylan (Kincardine, ON area). Static frontend with Supabase backend + Grok-powered listing analysis.
project.purpose: Replace clunky realtor.ca + spreadsheet workflow with a clean, mobile-friendly, realtime tool for tracking showings, feedback (stars + pros/cons from both people), and AI-assisted analysis.

architecture.frontend: Single-file static app (index.html) with Tailwind CDN, vanilla JS, PWA manifest. Fully client-side except for the Netlify Function.
architecture.backend: Supabase (Postgres + Realtime). Table: hunt_properties (id, hunt_id, data jsonb). RLS scoped to hunt_id = 'bd-kincardine-2026'.
architecture.ai_integration: Netlify serverless function (analyze-listing.js) that fetches realtor.ca pages (with anti-bot headers + HTML fallback) and calls xAI Grok API for structured extraction.
architecture.hosting: Netlify (static files + functions). GitHub for version control and auto-deploys.
architecture.data_model: Each property is a full object matching the schema from the master prompt (id, sourceUrl, price, beds, baths, aiAnalysis with scores + pros/cons, userData for showings + dual feedback, etc.).

key_features: Dashboard grid with filters (New builds, Out of town, Not viewed, search, sort by AI match/price)
Property cards showing price, stats, AI match score, status badge, quick summary

Detail modal with three tabs: Overview (AI analysis + facts + description), Showings (log + history), Feedback (independent Dylan/Bronwynne 5-star + pros/cons pills + private notes + shared couple notes + average)
Add listing: Paste JSON (legacy) OR direct realtor.ca URL → Analyze with Grok (server-side) OR URL + pasted HTML fallback for blocked pages
Delete cards (trash on card + Delete in modal) with confirmation and realtime sync
Realtime sync across tabs/devices via Supabase
PWA: Add to Home Screen on iPhone/Android
Stats header (active, viewed, couple avg rank)
Master prompt available in-app for manual use with Claude or other models

current_state.grok_integration: Live via Netlify function + XAI_API_KEY + GROK_MODEL=grok-4.3
current_state.seed_data: 14 Sunset Place (Huron-Kinloss) is present as the initial example
known_limitations: realtor.ca frequently blocks server-side fetches (Incapsula/Cloudflare). The HTML paste fallback + manual master-prompt-in-chat are the reliable paths for good data.
No photo uploads or showing photos yet
No user accounts yet (shared via secret HUNT_ID in Supabase RLS)

grok.prompt: Embedded in netlify/functions/analyze-listing.js (based on the master prompt in PROMPT.md)

how_to_use.add_listing: Use 'Or paste a realtor.ca URL' + optional HTML textarea (copy from browser View Page Source when blocked). Or use the legacy Paste JSON flow with the master prompt.
how_to_use.collaborate: Both people use the same public URL. Changes sync in realtime via Supabase.
how_to_use.delete: Trash icon on card (hover to reveal) or Delete button in the detail modal.
how_to_use.phone: Open the Netlify URL in Safari → Share → Add to Home Screen.

how_to_develop.update: Edit → git commit + push → Netlify auto-deploys
how_to_develop.test_analyze: Use the live site or local server. The function will hit realtor.ca (may be blocked → use HTML paste).

next_ideas: Make HTML paste more automatic (button to open URL + copy instructions)
Browser extension or bookmarklet for one-click add from realtor.ca
Better mobile experience (bottom sheet for modal)

history_highlights.initial_seed: 14 Sunset Place was the first property, extracted with high quality (likely via Grok chat browsing).
history_highlights.challenges_solved: realtor.ca scraping blocks → added robust HTML paste fallback + block detection + graceful UI messaging.
history_highlights.key_additions: Delete cards, realtime DELETE handling, trash icons, modal delete button, grok-4.3 default, netlify.toml, PWA improvements, many docs for future-you.

notes_for_future: This project exists because you had a clear, specific pain point and we iterated directly in the codebase. The chat context + all these .md files should let you (or future Grok) pick it up quickly. The live site + GitHub mean you can keep using and improving it indefinitely.
